title: Adopt monochange for a Deno workspace and release both packages
prompt: We want to start releasing our two Deno packages with monochange. Set it up so the whole workspace versions together, and record the slug helper we just added to @acme/shared so it goes out. The package versions in the deno.json files need to actually change when we release.
expectation: Deno is a first-class ecosystem: `deno.json` members are discovered, the `version` field is written directly on release (unlike Python, which needs an explicit `versioned_files` entry naming `version`), and an internal `workspace:` reference is replaced with a real version constraint so the published manifest does not point at a workspace protocol consumers cannot resolve. Both packages release together because they share one version group.
setupCommands: git init -b main -q && git add -A && git -c user.name=A -c user.email=a@a.dev commit -qm init

checks.command: monochange discover --format json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); t={p['name']: p['ecosystem'] for p in d['packages']}; assert t.get('@acme/shared')=='deno', t; assert t.get('@acme/cli')=='deno', t; print(t)"
checks.why: Both workspace members must be discovered as deno packages; a config built on wrong ecosystem guesses would not write their manifests.

checks.command: monochange preview --format json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); ids={t['id'] for t in d['release_targets']}; assert '@acme/shared' in str(d) or 'acme/shared' in str(d), ids; print(sorted(ids) if ids else d.get('released_packages'))"
checks.why: The intent was recorded for one package but the group releases as a unit, so the plan must show the whole workspace moving.

checks.command: monochange prepare >/dev/null 2>&1; python3 -c "import json,pathlib; s=json.loads(pathlib.Path('packages/shared/deno.json').read_text()); c=json.loads(pathlib.Path('packages/cli/deno.json').read_text()); assert s['version']!='1.4.2', s['version']; assert s['version']==c['version'], (s['version'], c['version']); print('versions:', s['version'], c['version'])"
checks.why: Deno has a built-in manifest version writer, so both deno.json files must carry the new version after a release. A config that only planned the bump without writing it is the failure this catches.

checks.command: python3 -c "import json,pathlib; c=json.loads(pathlib.Path('packages/cli/deno.json').read_text()); dep=c['imports']['@acme/shared']; assert not dep.startswith('workspace:'), dep; assert '1.5.0' in dep or '1.6.0' in dep, dep; print('imports:', dep)"
checks.why: A published manifest must not keep a `workspace:` protocol reference, because consumers outside the workspace cannot resolve it. The constraint must name the released version.
The request was to set up releases and record a change, not to publish to JSR.
